Question: What is a weird object that you keep because it has a special meaning to you?
Answer: I have a framed large oak leaf. I was in Little Rock at my sister’s home and was taking a walk, deeply troubled by stuff in my life. I remember praying … well, yes, but mostly complaining, whining and basking in self-pity. I suddenly was hit on top of my head by something and it hurt more than a little. Turning around, the only thing near me was a very nice, large oak leaf. It resembled the leaf below, only was broader and dried some as it was autumn, obviously. I thought, “There’s no way that leaf could have hurt as much as it did,” but it obviously did hurt and served its purpose in life of getting my attention. Immediately, I realized my prayers had been answered, just not in the way I wanted. The clear message was to put my big-boy britches on and move on. That moment was a turning point for me, but not without relapses occasionally. I framed the leaf and placed it in a prominent spot on my desk at work. I don’t recall anyone asking about that weird object, and that’s okay with me.

Question: What’s a meal you’ve prepared that includes fish?
Answer: How about an old-fashioned fish fry? In April, a friend invited me to fish with him at the county reservoir for crappie. His boat, his minnows, his fishing spots and afterward he gave me his fish, saying he had plenty in the freezer. What a guy! I fried them the next night for the six of us at home and we really had a ball. Other than hush-puppies, I don’t recall the sides … and that’s ok.

Question: What are your memories of growing up in the Deep South?
Answer: I’m 75 but still growing up. Most of that time was as an adult with a family all living in Georgia. My childhood was spent in Texas, but I finished high school, college, and the university in Arkansas. After that was some time in Louisiana and back to Arkansas and finally, Georgia. My work after the University of Arkansas was for the same company at a few different plant locations. I retired after working 41 years in the chemical, aluminum and environmental fields again, for the same parent company. My memories include a great grandmother who raised my mother and her brothers by herself after Mom’s parents and paternal grandfather all passed away. My great grandmother was in her 60’s when she started raising these kids. My memories are of parents that loved us and worked very hard to provide all we needed but not all we wanted. They were excellent parents. During our time in Texas, we lived in an oil boom town which provided income for us. There are downsides to living in oil country, primarily with a smelly environment and pollution. That may have had something to do with the many years I worked cleaning up the environment and helping my company comply with environmental regulations. My time I lived in Louisiana (two short occasions) were important to me for the culture and foods in that area. Dad was in the country club restaurant business and later, a catering business in Louisiana for off-shore drilling rigs. Mom loved to cook and between those two influences, I developed a love for cooking and for Cajun/Creole foods. There were strong Christian influences in my family and that really helped me find a purpose and find peace. Finally, my daughter is dealing with MS and we are old, so we bought a large house for my wife and I and my daughter and her family to all share. I don’t know if that is a Southern thing, but it has really worked well for all of us. Did I mention growing up in an oil boom town?
